publications.title: Katsina Economic Linkage & Capability Model (KELCM): Synergizing Resources for Lasting Impact
publications.abstract: Authored by Mohammed Labaran Sani, the Katsina Economic Linkage and Capability Model (KELCM) synthesizes Amartya Sen's Capability Approach, Albert Hirschman's Theory of Economic Linkages, and Jeffrey Sachs' Comprehensive Development Approach into a three-pillar operational model for Katsina State's 34 Local Government Areas (>8 million residents)—connecting human capital (education, healthcare, empowerment) with strategic sectoral investments (agro-processing clusters, sustainable mining, solar/wind energy, and transport/water infrastructure).
publications.full_description: Presents a comprehensive sub-national economic and sustainable development architecture for Katsina State, Nigeria. Anchored in Sen's Capability Approach, Hirschman's backward/forward sectoral linkages, and Sachs' SDG-integrated development strategy, KELCM outlines actionable plans across Pillar I (Human Capital Development: rural school upgrades, vocational training, primary healthcare & mobile clinics, social safety nets, and women/youth microfinance), Pillar II (Strategic Sectoral Investment: modernized irrigation and agro-processing clusters for millet, rice, and groundnuts; environmentally regulated mining; solar and wind power; and transport/water infrastructure), and Pillar III (Integrated & Sustainable Development: multi-sectoral programmes, Public-Private Partnerships, and SDG monitoring).

publications.title: Addressing Five Structural Gaps in African Climate Education Systems: Policy Recommendations for Governments
publications.abstract: Climate shocks already interrupt learning across Africa—disrupting 20 million students in West, Central, Eastern, and Southern Africa in 2024 and causing US$1.3 billion in direct education damage (2005–2024)—yet education systems remain under-equipped. This brief synthesizes UNESCO, UNICEF, IPCC AR6, and NAP Global Network data across five gaps (curricula, teacher readiness, resilient schools, climate finance, and African-led research) and sets out a sequenced government action matrix.
publications.full_description: Examines five binding constraints on climate-resilient education in Africa: (1) 47% of national curriculum frameworks make no reference to climate change; (2) fewer than 30% of teachers feel ready to teach it; (3) floods and heatwaves cost learners 18 school days per year while every US$1 in resilient school construction saves US$2–13 in avoided losses; (4) only 1.5% of climate finance reaches education and only 27% of NAPs cost education actions; and (5) Africa-related topics receive at most 3.8% of global climate research funding (only 14.5% to African institutions). Provides a 0–3 year sequenced reform roadmap for Ministries of Education, Finance, Environment, and Works.

publications.title: Umaru Musa Fellowship Initiative (UMFI): Project Proposal for Youth Leadership, Education & Decent Jobs
publications.abstract: A flagship future initiative we hope to spearhead in honour of late President Umaru Musa Yar'Adua. UMFI is designed as an intensive 8-week leadership, mentorship, policy research, and civic engagement fellowship for 45 emerging youth leaders (ages 20–35) across Education, Decent Jobs, and Public Service in Katsina State and Nigeria.
publications.full_description: Full project proposal dossier for the Umaru Musa Fellowship Initiative (UMFI) — 'Empower. Innovate. Transform.' Outlines the problem statement, 8-week innovation design, mission and vision, 10 programme objectives, target demographic (youth aged 20–35 across 6 sector profiles), dual benefits to participants and State Government, 16-stage operational lifecycle, 45-fellow residential/field equipment specification, risk mitigation matrix, and 7-part long-term sustainability strategy.

publications.title: Africa by 2063: Assessing Progress and Priorities for the Decade Ahead
publications.abstract: Ten years into Agenda 2063, Africa has built most of the continental scaffolding—AfCFTA (54 signatories, 48 ratifications), SAATM (37 states), the Free Movement Protocol, and the AU G20 seat—yet national ratification and delivery lag behind. Synthesizing IMF, AfDB, UNCTAD, OECD/AUC/ATAF, ITU, and WMO data across five visual charts and seven regional case figures, this brief proposes six targeted priorities for the Second Ten-Year Implementation Plan (2024–2033).
publications.full_description: Co-authored by Mohammed Labaran Sani and Mahamat H. Mahamat (26 November 2026), this flagship policy brief audits the First Ten-Year Implementation Plan (2014–2023) of the African Union's Agenda 2063 and sets out measurable priorities for the Second Ten-Year Implementation Plan (2024–2033). It examines structural transformation (4.4% GDP growth vs. 10.6% manufacturing share), AfCFTA corridors, the Free Movement ratification bottleneck (4 of 15 ratifications), domestic revenue and debt service (16.1% tax-to-GDP vs. 31% revenue absorbed by external debt service), climate adaptation costs ($30–50B/year), and human capital for Africa's 12 million annual youth labor entrants.

publications.title: A Permanent Seat for Africa: Reforming the UN Security Council
publications.abstract: More than eighty years after the founding of the United Nations, Africa has no permanent seat on the Security Council—despite accounting for 54 of 193 UN member states (28%), roughly 18% of global population, around half of all Council meetings, 70% of Chapters VI/VII resolutions with peace-operation mandates, and over 40% of UN uniformed peacekeepers. This brief evaluates the Ezulwini Consensus, the Sirte Declaration, and five reform steps toward the 2028 UN Charter review horizon.
publications.full_description: Authored by Mohammed Labaran Sani (26 November 2026), this policy brief analyzes the structural exclusion of Africa from permanent representation on the United Nations Security Council. Drawing on Security Council Report datasets, UN Peacekeeping troop statistics, the 2005 Ezulwini Consensus and Sirte Declaration, Action 39 of the September 2024 Pact for the Future, and recent P5 positions, it compares the AU common position against the G4, Uniting for Consensus (UfC), and US-backed proposals, and sets out five concrete policy steps for the AU, Committee of Ten (C-10), and P5 members.

publications.title: Nature-Based Solutions as a Preventive and Disaster Risk Reduction Strategy for the Alau Dam Flood Disaster in Maiduguri, Nigeria
publications.abstract: Triggered by prolonged heavy rainfall and the collapse of the Alau Dam in September 2024, flooding inundated over 40% of Maiduguri Municipal Council, killing 37 people, injuring 58, and displacing more than 414,000 residents (ACAPS, 2024; IOM, 2024). This policy brief demonstrates how watershed restoration, afforestation, wetland conservation, sustainable land management, and Vetiver grass (Chrysopogon zizanioides) bioengineering can complement dam rehabilitation to build long-term flood resilience.
publications.full_description: Authored by Mohammed Labaran Sani, this policy brief examines the compound drivers of the September 2024 Alau Dam flood disaster in Borno State, Nigeria—where aging dam infrastructure, sediment accumulation, and limited spillway capacity combined with upstream catchment deforestation and wetland encroachment. Drawing on empirical soil-and-water conservation evidence (Oku, Asubonteng & Blege, 2015; IUCN, 2020; World Bank, 2017), it outlines a 6-part integrated green-grey flood risk reduction strategy for Federal and Borno State Ministries, the Chad Basin Development Authority, NEMA, and SEMA.

publications.title: Lingua Franca—Ing Hausa into Climate: Linguistic Accessibility and Inclusive Climate Governance
publications.abstract: Nearly 90% of global scientific publications are in English, creating a two-tier system in Northern Nigeria between those who can read climate science and those who live with its consequences. Drawing on Afrobarometer awareness data (only 30% awareness in Nigeria; 26% rural; 23% women) and evaluations of Hausa farm radio (In Kidi ya Chanza) and voice advisories reaching 97% farmer trust, this brief proposes six policy actions to institutionalize Hausa climate terminology, translation, and education across 94 million speakers.
publications.full_description: Examines how linguistic exclusion breaks the chain of climate governance at its very first link. Despite ₦200.6 million allocated to federal climate awareness over four years under Nigeria's National Climate Change Policy (2021–2030), rural Hausa-speaking communities remain underserved by uncontextualized English messaging. Sets out a six-part roadmap: establishing a standard Hausa climate glossary panel, translating policies and early warnings, integrating Hausa into school/university curricula, strengthening vernacular media, piloting participatory community communication, and building cross-border West African partnerships.

publications.title: EL NIÑO: Me Ya Kamata Kowane Ɗan Najeriya Ya Sani? (Hausa Super El Niño Public Advisory)
publications.abstract: Abin da ke faruwa a Tekun Pacific na iya shafar rayuwarmu a Najeriya. Wannan takardar bayani cikin harshen Hausa tana fassara kimiyyar guguwar yanayi ta Super El Niño (+3.3°C Niño 3.4 a Oktoba 2026), hasashen NiMet kan ambaliya a jihohin Arewa da ƙarancin ruwa a Kudu, haɗarin tsananin zafi (31,400), da matakan kariya ga manoma, iyalai, al'umma da hukumomin lafiya.
publications.full_description: Published entirely in Hausa to bridge the climate science communication gap across Northern Nigeria and the Sahel, this public educational brief explains the ocean-atmospheric mechanics of the 2026–2027 Super El Niño. It synthesizes WMO, NOAA, Columbia University CCSR/IRI (+3.3°C anomaly), NiMet state-by-state rainfall projections, and NEMA's October 25, 2026 preparedness directives into actionable guidance for farmers, households, communities, and local governments.

publications.title: From Subsidy Removal to Public Accountability: Making Nigeria's Fuel Reform Work for Households by 2030
publications.abstract: Nigeria's May 2023 subsidy removal and FX unification mobilised ₦15.8 trillion for the Federation by December 2025, yet only ₦5.43 trillion reached the Federal Government while new borrowing supplied 58% of incremental resources. By mid-2027, the Ministry of Finance and National Cash Transfer Office should publish quarterly, disaggregated fiscal and social reports reconciled to audited accounts under Section 30 of the Fiscal Responsibility Act 2007.
publications.full_description: Independent policy analysis examining the fiscal, regional price, and household social-protection outcomes of Nigeria's May 2023 petrol subsidy removal and foreign-exchange unification. Drawing on the Federal Ministry of Finance's August 2026 Reform Scorecard, World Bank Nigeria Development Updates, Auditor-General findings, and National Bureau of Statistics PMS Price Watch series through 2026, this brief sets out four statutory accountability milestones and a 2027–2030 minimum reporting standard across federal, state, and local governments.

publications.title: Rethinking Climate Finance for Africa
publications.abstract: Co-authored by Mohammed Labaran Sani and Amina Baala (baalaamina@gmail.com). Africa requires approximately USD 2.8 trillion between 2020 and 2030 to implement 51 Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), yet climate finance flows reached only $44 billion in 2021/22 (23% of annual need), with more than half arriving as debt. This brief evaluates debt-for-nature swaps, concessional capital guarantees, and the Second Africa Climate Summit's Addis Ababa Declaration to propose seven grant-equivalent delivery reforms.
publications.full_description: Examines why the structure of African climate finance—not just its volume—is the binding constraint on resilience. Against US$865 billion in decadal African external debt service and borrowing costs two to three times higher than in advanced economies, the brief analyzes Gabon's $500M Blue Bond, IEA concessional leverage multipliers, the African Climate Facility, and the Loss and Damage Fund, setting out seven concrete benchmarks for negotiators through 2035.

publications.title: Adapting Rotterdam’s Sponge City Model for Urban Flood Resilience in Lagos
publications.abstract: Following July 2026 flash floods across 15 Lagos communities, state suspension of land reclamation, and tidal locking caused by a one-metre lagoon rise, this brief evaluates which elements of Rotterdam's Sponge City model (such as the 1.7-million-litre Benthemplein water square) can be adapted to Lagos. It recommends permanent statutory wetland protection, desilting maintenance across 1,500 km of channels, flap gates/pumps for tidal locking, and three resident-co-designed mainland pilot water squares in Kosofe, Ikeja, or Agege.
publications.full_description: Satellite analysis from 1984 to 2023 reveals a 38% expansion in Lagos' built-up area alongside a 32% loss of forests and 11% reduction in water bodies, placing over 60% of urban Lagos at risk of extreme flooding by 2050. Comparing Rotterdam's Benthemplein water square and cancelled Bloemhofplein trial against Lagos' land scarcity, informal settlement vulnerability, and tidal locking, this policy brief distinguishes cost-effective grey-green infrastructure and statutory floodplain protection from prestige spending.

publications.title: URGENT POLICY BRIEF: 31,400 Lives at Risk? Nigeria's Race Against Super El Niño
publications.abstract: Comprehensive heat-health vulnerability assessment and sub-national early warning policy directives ahead of the projected 2026–2027 Super El Niño cycle across Northern Nigeria.
publications.full_description: Between September 2026 and February 2027, predictive ocean-atmospheric telemetry indicates a severe Super El Niño phase coinciding with dry season ambient temperature spikes across the West African Sahel. Without proactive, community-anchored heat-health adaptation protocols, epidemiological models project up to 31,400 excess heat-vulnerability events across Northern Nigeria.
